Do you think a million-dollar term life insurance policy sounds like too much insurance?

As a Certified Financial Planner, I see underinsured people every day.

A million-dollar term life insurance policy might actually be the minimum coverage needed for the typical middle-class household, but it’s affordable.

That might sound like an exaggeration, but if you crunch the numbers – just as we’ll be doing a little bit – you’ll realize that a million-dollar policy might be just what you need.

The good news is term life insurance isn’t nearly as costly as most people think.

In a recent development, what makes term life insurance even better is that larger policies cost less on a per thousand basis than smaller policies do. You may find the premium on a $1 million policy is only a little bit higher than it is for $500,000.

Probably, but let’s find out. A general rule of thumb is that you should get 10x your income as baseline coverage for life insurance.

If you’re young, that may be low because you may want to provide your family with enough to replace your income for 15 years or more.

Today, $1 million has become the newly introduced baseline for life insurance by a primary breadwinner. Anything less could leave your family financially impaired.

Here’s a list of all the different obligations you may want to have life insurance cover in the unfortunate event you pass away early.

Now that you have an idea of these obligations, let’s punch them into this life insurance calculator to find out if you need a million-dollar policy.

In a recent development, according to Policy Genius, the average cost for a 20-year $1 million term life insurance policy for a 35-year-old male is $53 per month. However, your rate will vary according to the following factors.

The best, and easiest place to start is online. I recommend having two or three insurers compete for your business to make sure you get the best rate and coverage. To see how cheap term life can be, choose your state from the map above to be matched with top life insurance providers instantly.

Let’s look at the individual components that can quickly add up to over a million-dollar policy.

This is where things can get a bit intimidating. Even if you earn a modest income, you may need close to $1 million to replace that income after your death in order to provide for your family’s basic living expenses.

The conventional wisdom in the insurance industry is that you should maintain a life insurance policy equal to between 10 times and 20 times your annual income. So if you earn around $50K per year, that would mean policy coverage between $500K and $1 million.

The complication today is that with interest rates being as low as they are that might not be enough either.

For example, if you have a $1 million policy that could be invested at 5% per year, your family could live on the interest earned – which conveniently comes to $50,000 per year – for the next 20 years.

Sources indicate that that would still leave the original $1 million intact to cover other expenses. But with today’s microscopic interest rates, there’s no way to get a guaranteed return of 5% on your money, certainly not for 15 or 20 years.

According to recent reports, also, keep in mind that most insurance companies have a maximum multiplier you can apply to your income for life insurance coverage. For example, it wouldn’t make much sense for a 22-year-old making $27,000 per year to get a $2 million life insurance. Or a 65-year-old that is retired to secure a $3 million dollar policy.

The table below is approximately how much you’re allowed to multiply your income based on your age and income:.

Using the table above as a guide, a 35-year-old making $150,000 per year would be capped at taking out a $4.5 million term policy ($150,000 x 30 = $4,500,000).

Here we start with the basics – wrapping up your final affairs.

According to recent reports, this will include funeral costs and any lingering medical costs. A reasonable estimate for a typical funeral is around $20,000.

Industry observers note that crazy, right? You can get burial insurance to cover only the most basic of final expenses.

Sources indicate that debt burdens are high in the US, and debt can be especially crushing on remaining family members. Many life insurance customers make sure they can pay off most of their debt with the policy.

Medical costs are a serious variable. Even if you have excellent health insurance, there are likely to be unpaid medical bills lingering after your death. This has to do with copayments, deductibles, and coinsurance provisions.

Sources indicate that collectively, they can add up to many thousands of dollars. But where things get really complicated is if you die of a terminal illness.

For example, if you are stricken by an illness that lasts for several years, you could incur a number of expenses that are not covered by insurance. This may include the cost of personal care and even experimental treatments.

A home may be a large asset, but it’s also often a homeowner’s largest debt. The average mortgage balance in the US is roughly $236,443 according to Experian data. So you could easily use a life insurance policy to pay off that debt and relieve your loved ones of a monthly mortgage payment.

Recent findings suggest that credit card debt and other personal debt are some of the most expensive obligations carrying rates upward of 20% in some cases. Make sure you have enough to cover this very expensive debt.

Below is a sampling of major expenses your family is likely to incur, either on an annual basis or at some point after your death.

Tuition costs continue to skyrocket. The Department of Education suggests that four-year public college tuition has been rising an average of 5% per year, far exceeding the rate of inflation. If you have one child who attends an in-state public school, a second at an out-of-state public school, and a third in a private university, the total expenditure will reach $416,560.

Industry observers note that vehicles and other forms of transportation represent another large sum. Unfortunately, with increasing electronics and safety features, the average cost of a new car continues to grow.

It has been revealed that if your family relies on your work for healthcare, take notice. According to eHealth.com, the average health insurance premium for a family is $22,221. That’s a shade under $2,000 per month in additional cost. This cost will only rise, and the need could last for years.

So far, we’ve been describing the financial obligations likely to affect a typical household.But there may be certain situations that will produce obligations that are less obvious.

For example, if you’re a business owner, there may be debts or other financial obligations that will need to be paid upon your death.

Even though no one in your family may be qualified or interested in taking over your business, the payoff of those obligations may be completely necessary to enable the sale of the business.

Another possibility is that you’re a real estate investor.

If your properties are heavily indebted, extra insurance proceeds may be necessary either to carry the properties until they’re sold, or even to pay off existing indebtedness to free up cash flow for income.

You may even need additional funds if you are taking care of an extended family member, like an aging parent.

These are just some of the many possibilities of expenses that will need to be covered by insurance proceeds.

Before we move on to specific life insurance quotes, let’s first consider the factors that affect term life insurance premiums.

This is typically the single most important premium factor. The older you are, the more likely you are to die within the term of the policy.

Industry observers note that this is a close second and why it’s so vital to apply for a policy as early in life as possible. Premiums on life insurances rates literally increase by each year.

It has been revealed that if you have any health conditions that may affect mortality, such as diabetes or hypertension, your premiums will be higher. This is another compelling reason to apply while you are young and in good health.

It’s not that policies are not available to people with health conditions, it’s just that they’re less expensive if you don’t have any.

Size of the policy matters, but not the way you might think. Yes, a $1 million policy will cost more than a $500,000 policy. But it won’t cost twice as much.

Air France-KLM's Flying Blue program runs what they call **Promo Rewards** — a monthly flash sale on award seats that slashes the points price by 25 to 50% on select routes. In Business class, that can mean seats that would normally cost 80,000+ miles dropping to as low as 40,000 miles one-way. On a route where a cash ticket retails for $3,000, you're extracting **7.5 cents per point** — and on premium routes during peak travel periods, that figure can climb to 15 cents per point. If you have 40,000 transferable points sitting in a Chase or Amex account, this is the difference between a $400 economy ticket and a $3,000 business class experience — for the same points. The pricing inefficiency exists because Flying Blue uses these promotional awards as a marketing tool to fill premium cabin seats on specific dates that might otherwise go out with empty seats. Airlines would rather have a loyalist in that seat than fly it empty. You, as someone who's built a transferable points balance, are perfectly positioned to take advantage of the moment they make that trade-off. This isn't a loophole that's about to close. Flying Blue has run Promo Rewards consistently for years. It's a **structural feature of the program** — one the ChooseFI community can build an annual travel strategy around. The challenge isn't finding the deal. It's being ready when it drops.

The mechanism behind Flying Blue Promo Rewards is elegantly simple once you understand it, and it separates this program from virtually every other airline loyalty play in your toolkit.

Flying Blue Has a Dynamic Award Chart — With a Monthly Override.

It has been revealed that flying Blue moved to dynamic pricing, which typically means the program is less predictable and often less valuable than the old fixed-chart days. But here's where it gets interesting: Promo Rewards operate as a fixed-price overlay on top of that dynamic system. On the 1st of each month (or within the first few days), Flying Blue publishes a curated list of routes — often 20 to 40 city pairs — with fixed, deeply discounted mile prices. Business class seats on transatlantic routes regularly appear at 40,000 to 50,000 miles one-way. These are not dynamic prices that will creep up as demand increases. They're locked promotional rates on specific routes.

This means the program essentially gives you two separate games to play: the chaotic dynamic pricing game (usually skip it), and the monthly Promo Rewards game (always pay attention).

The Fuel Surcharge Nuance You Must Know.

According to recent reports, flying Blue does pass on carrier-imposed surcharges for standard awards on Air France and KLM flights — this can add $200 to $500 to what should be a points redemption. But here's the critical detail: Promo Reward bookings eliminate those surcharges. You pay the miles, a small booking fee, and that's it. This is a significant hidden value that casual points users miss entirely. The published cash price comparison becomes even more favorable once you factor in that you're not paying the surcharge on top.

Don't be in a position where you need to wait on a credit card statement to close before you can transfer.

Do This: Use Open-Jaw Routing to Maximize Your Trip.

Flying Blue allows open-jaw routing. Book into Paris (CDG) and out of Amsterdam (AMS) — or any combination of Air France/KLM hub cities — and you've just built a multi-country European trip into a single award booking. This is the kind of routing flexibility that turns a one-city trip into a proper adventure.

Do This: Track Multiple Months of Route Patterns.

According to recent reports, promo routes rotate monthly, but certain routes appear repeatedly — particularly transatlantic and routes between European hubs and Africa or the Middle East. After 2–3 months of observation, you'll start to recognize patterns and can initiative your travel around routes that are likely to repeat.

Avoid This: Transferring Points Before Confirming Availability.

According to recent reports, this is the single biggest mistake beginners make. Always confirm the specific flight, date, and cabin availability before transferring points. Miles are a one-way street — you cannot transfer them back. If availability disappears after you've transferred, you're left with Flying Blue miles that may not be useful for your target route at standard (non-Promo) pricing.

Avoid This: Ignoring Standard Award Pricing.

In a recent development, flying Blue's dynamic pricing outside of Promo Rewards can be punishingly expensive. A Business class seat that costs 40,000 Promo miles might cost 90,000+ miles at standard dynamic pricing. Always wait for the Promo if you can — patience pays.

According to recent reports, the ideal earning setup for this redemption combines a Chase Sapphire Reserve (3x on travel and dining, instant transfer to Flying Blue) with an Amex Gold or Platinum (4x on dining/groceries or 5x on flights respectively, also instant transfer). Between two cards, you can accumulate 40,000–80,000 points in a single year of normal household spending.

Best For: Flexible Couples and Solo Travelers Who Proposal in Advance.

In a recent development, this redemption is purpose-built for the FI community member who thinks in systems, not spontaneous splurges. You're someone who has already built a transferable points balance of at least 40,000–80,000 points across Chase Ultimate Rewards, Amex Membership Rewards, or Citi ThankYou — and who can act decisively when the right route appears.

In a recent development, couples are the sweet spot. Two people, two Business class seats, one incredible transatlantic experience. Solo travelers benefit enormously too — a single seat at 40,000 miles is one of the highest-CPP solo redemptions in the entire transferable points ecosystem.

According to recent reports, minimum Viable Setup: 40,000 Flying Blue miles or 40,000 transferable points in Chase, Amex, or Citi. A Flying Blue account with verified transfer links. The flexibility to travel within a 30-day window of whatever routes appear that month.

Sources indicate that create a free Flying Blue account at flyingblue.com and enable email notifications. Keep at least 40,000 to 80,000 transferable points in your Chase, Amex, Citi, Capital One, or Bilt account. Set a recurring calendar reminder for the 1st of each month.

Recent findings suggest that visit flyingblue.com on the morning of the 1st (or within the first few days) to see the latest Promo Rewards routes. Scan for destinations that match your interests. Note the discounted mile pricing and travel date windows — promos typically cover travel within the next 2 to 3 months.

Use the Flying Blue award search to check specific dates on the promo routes in business class. Confirm that seats are available at the promo price before you transfer any points. The calendar view lets you scan across multiple dates swiftly.

Transfer the required miles from Chase (instant), Amex (1-2 days), Citi (instant), Capital One (1-2 days), or Bilt (1-2 days). Book on flyingblue.com the moment your miles arrive. Do not wait — promo availability is limited and the best dates disappear within hours.

Promo Rewards typically offer 25 to 50 percent off standard dynamic pricing. A business class transatlantic award that normally costs 80,000 to 100,000 miles one-way can drop to 40,000 to 50,000 miles on a Promo Reward. Additionally, fuel surcharges are eliminated on promo awards, saving another $100 to $300 per ticket that would otherwise be charged on standard awards.

According to recent reports, chase Ultimate Rewards and Citi ThankYou are the best because they transfer instantly to Flying Blue at a 1:1 ratio. Amex Membership Rewards and Capital One both transfer at 1:1 but take 1 to 2 business days. Bilt also transfers at 1:1. Since promo availability is time-sensitive, instant transfer partners give you a meaningful speed advantage.

It has been revealed that yes. Promo Rewards rotate destinations each month and cover specific travel date windows, typically 2 to 3 months out. You cannot choose which routes are discounted. The strategy works best for travelers who have a list of destinations they want to visit and can match those against whatever promos appear each month rather than needing a specific route on a specific date.

The best routes with the best dates typically sell out within 24 to 48 hours of the monthly announcement. Business class availability is particularly limited. Set a reminder for the 1st of each month and check within the first few hours of the announcement for the widest selection of dates and routes.

According to recent reports, this sweet spot was last verified over 90 days ago. Award availability and pricing may have changed — verify current rates before booking.

Flying Blue Promo Rewards is the most repeatable sweet spot in travel rewards because it renews every single month. While other sweet spots are one-time plays or annual opportunities, Promo Rewards gives you 12 chances per year to book premium cabin flights at 25 to 50 percent off standard pricing with no fuel surcharges. The system rewards exactly the kind of behavior the FI community already excels at: preparation, patience, and decisive action when the numbers align. Keep 40,000 to 80,000 transferable points in reserve, check on the 1st of every month, and book the moment you find a route that matches your travel list. Over time, this single strategy can deliver thousands of dollars in business class experiences at economy-level points costs.

In a recent development, choose the budgeting app that fits the way your money comes in, and pay as little as you can. If financial aid has to last the whole term, get YNAB, free for a year to verified college students. If you’re paid by the hour, Goodbudget’s free plan lets you divide each paycheck among spending categories.

YNAB charges everyone else $109 a year, and each student gets the free year only once, not every year of school. To claim it, submit proof that you’re enrolled, such as a student ID, a transcript, or a tuition statement.

The other picks all have free plans except Qapital, which charges $3 a month after a 30-day free trial. Each does one job best for a student, from splitting rent with roommates to saving automatically.

It lets you assign a semester’s aid to each month the money must cover before you spend any, and by YNAB’s estimate, approving the purchases it imports takes a couple of minutes a day.

For more information, read our full YNAB Review.

First-time budgeters can learn zero-based budgeting, planning every dollar of income before the month starts, without ever paying, as long as they’ll type in each purchase.

For more information, read our full EveryDollar Review.

If your hours change week to week, collect your paychecks first, then fill digital envelopes, one per spending category, once you know what came in.

For more information, read our full Goodbudget Review.

Link your bank account and Cleo’s free tools track your spending and help you set a budget, with no purchases to type in, and you can ask Cleo about your money in chat.

For more information, read our full Cleo Review.

Roommates each log what they paid toward rent and utilities, and Splitwise keeps a running balance of who owes whom.

For more information, read our full Splitwise Review.

Students who forget to save can set rules once, and Qapital moves money into savings goals on its own, such as a share of each paycheck the day it’s deposited.

For more information, read our full Qapital Review.

Industry observers note that on a student budget, the right app fits how your money comes in and costs little or nothing. Use YNAB’s free year to make a semester’s aid last, and before the year ends, decide whether to pay $109 a year or move to a free proposal.

Sources indicate that are you trying to win the Mega Millions, but your numbers never seem to come up? It may be time to look for better ways to make money. Fortunately, you can earn extra cash without going and getting a “real job.”.

What are the best ways to avoid sitting in a cubicle all day? Some money-making strategies require an upfront investment, while others let you earn money in your free time with the help of apps.

Read on to learn the best ways to earn cash without a regular 9-5 job, plus tips on how almost anyone can get started.

One of the easiest ways to earn money is by signing up to participate in market research studies. You won’t make much, a few dollars here and there, but you can create a free account and get started within minutes.

You’ll be paid in PayPal cash or gift cards for sharing your opinion and completing other tasks online.

Industry observers note that E-Poll Market Research is one of the top companies to consider for this type of work. They make it easy to create an account and answer survey questions.

However, there are plenty of other options to consider, including:.

While market research gigs won’t make you rich, it’s something you can do during your spare time.

If you have a book idea, turning your story into an eBook can help you earn passive income without a regular job. Kindle Direct Publishing can even help you format your book for Kindle, at which point you can market and sell your book to millions of potential readers who shop on Amazon.com.

It has been revealed that how much can you earn writing eBooks? That depends on how many books you write, how much you sell them for, and how successful you are at marketing your book. Selling 20 books per month with a profit of $7 per book would net you $140 per month and $1,680 per year.

Industry observers note that meanwhile, selling 100 books per month at $7 per book would net you $700 per month and $8,400 per year. Need a little inspiration? Here’s an article that indicates you how to make your first $1,000 selling eBooks.

You can earn a lot of money by starting a blog or niche website and monetizing it. I should know. I started Good Financial Cents more than a decade ago, and have earned millions of dollars through the monetization of this site since its earliest days.

Recent findings suggest that how do you make money blogging? Earning real income with a website isn’t as easy as it looks, but there are plenty of monetization strategies you can try.

Here are the most common ways blogs make money:.

Recent findings suggest that if you’re curious about what it takes to earn money blogging, consider signing up for my Make 1K Challenge. It’s free and can help you earn your first $1,000 online with some of the blog monetization strategies I’ve already mentioned.

Industry observers note that you could argue that freelance work is like a regular job, but working at home and on your terms is much different from traditional employment. The fact is, most freelancers are fully remote – they can work from anywhere in the world with a laptop and an internet connection.

Plus, they can hire and fire clients based on their personal needs and preferences, and their income potential is unlimited. According to ZipRecruiter, freelancers in the U.S. average $63.53 per hour.

It has been revealed that of course, you’ll need a marketable skill to find paid work as a freelancer. This could be freelance writing, design skills, marketing expertise, or something else.

You can use several websites to market your skills as a freelancer, including:.

It has been revealed that healthyWage makes it possible to earn money while you lose weight. You won’t earn a ton of cash through the app, but you can earn a few dollars and use it to supplement other income you have.

The more weight you lose, the more money you can make. For example, the HealthyWage website claims some of their clients who lost more than 100 pounds managed to earn anywhere from $1,400 to $3,000.

However, the HW weight loss calculator reveals potential earnings of $578 to $828 for people who only have 15 pounds to lose.

In a recent development, if you have a car you rarely use and want to earn some side income, you can consider renting it out with Turo, a ride-sharing platform that connects car owners with people who need a short-term rental. You can set your price, although you’ll have more success if you price your car competitively.

Recent findings suggest that nicer vehicles in high-demand areas can easily fetch rates that surpass $100 per day through this platform. Turo notes that in-demand cars rented out regularly can bring in anywhere from $10,000 to $20,000 per year in net profit.

Plus, almost anyone can rent out their car provided it meets the guidelines of the Turo platform. Your car must be 12 years old or newer with less than 130,000 miles. It must be worth less than $200,000 (no Lambo’s), and you must also meet Turo’s auto insurance requirements.

Do you have a spare bedroom in your home that you never use? Maybe you have a basement or garage apartment you could fix up and begin renting for a profit?

Recent findings suggest that either way, Airbnb lets you rent out rooms and other spaces in your home on any dates you prefer. You must let renters know they’re renting a room in a home vs. an entire apartment or house and provide as much additional detail as possible.

The amount you can earn will depend on where you live and the type of accommodation you can offer. However, expensive cities like Chicago, New York, and San Francisco have plenty of rooms for rent that go for well over $100 per night.

You may not have an entire room you can rent, but even if you have some storage space, Neighbor.com allows you to rent it out to others in need.

Common spaces rented through this platform include.

In a recent development, the Neighbor.com platform makes it easy to advertise your unused space so that people nearby can inquire if they’re interested. Also, note that the platform offers insurance that can protect you if some of your client’s items are damaged or stolen while in your care.

According to recent reports, how much can you make renting out extra space? It depends on how much space you have to rent and where it’s located. However, Neighbor.com indicates a range of rental space options that cost anywhere from $20 to $100+ per month.

Industry observers note that investing in dividend stocks is one of the best ways to earn money without a regular job. Many early retirees find a way to live and pay bills based solely on the dividends they receive from various stocks.

It has been revealed that but what exactly is a dividend stock? For the most part, they are regular stocks but with a track record of sharing their profits with investors through dividends.

Dividends can also be earned in exchange-traded funds (ETFs) or mutual funds, and they can be significant once you build up a large portfolio.

Since dividends are paid by profitable companies, they tend to be seen as less risky for investors. If you’re curious about what it takes to get started with this strategy, this post explains how to invest in dividend stocks.

According to recent reports, housesitting is an option if you’re somewhat mobile and can move from place to place. Generally, you can find house-sitting gigs through word of mouth, referrals, or online portals like Craigslist.org or Facebook Marketplace.

It has been revealed that that said, not all house-sitting gigs are paid. Some offer the potential for exotic travel instead and free lodging for a week to several months.

In a recent development, either way, a website called TrustedHousesitters is the best place to find house-sitting gigs. Some jobs posted are for house-sitting only, while others require house sitters to provide basic care for pets or plants.

If you have serious wanderlust and want to travel far and wide, this platform can help make it happen. Many gigs posted online are in countries like Australia, Ireland, France, and Switzerland.

If you love animals and want to earn money taking care of them, several platforms can help turn your dream into a reality.

It has been revealed that for example, Rover.com lets you provide basic care for dogs or cats in your home, or you can pick up dog walking gigs. Another mobile app, called Wag!, lets you do more of the same.

You can set your rates for all types of work through these platforms, and your availability. While earnings vary by location and job, most people watch dogs and cats for anywhere from $40 to $100 per night.

Real estate investing may seem like a pipe dream if you hope to earn income without a job but hear me out. There are many ways to earn income through real estate without owning physical property or dealing with the hassles of being a landlord.

You can invest in real estate investment trusts (REITs) that let you build wealth over time. You can also use a platform called Fundrise to invest in real estate with a minimum investment of $10.

Fundrise lets you purchase eREITs, large investment funds that acquire, own, or operate multi-residential and commercial properties. The income you earn is entirely passive since it handles the work of finding income-producing properties and managing them.

In a recent development, while returns are never guaranteed, Fundrise investors have achieved very solid returns. Investors who use the platform earned an average return of 7.31% in 2020, followed by 22.99% in 2021, 1.50% in 2022 and -7.45% in 2023 (their first down year).

You can earn income on your spare change by investing it using Acorns. The roundup savings app syncs to your debit or credit card rounds up every purchase you make to the nearest dollar, and invests the difference. Once it’s set up, there’s no work on your part.

Most of the money is invested in ETFs and managed by the world’s top investment firms like Vanguard and BlackRock. While this app makes it easy to invest small amounts of money, it’s not free to use. Personal looks start at $3 per month, while a family initiative costs just $5.

If you’re looking for some paid gigs that are relatively easy, consider setting up a profile on TaskRabbit, an online platform that lets you get paid for completing various tasks, such as:.

In a recent development, projects typically pay between $30 and $100, although some pay significantly more than that. TaskRabbit also lets you pick and choose the jobs you want to take on based on your availability so that you can work entirely on your schedule.

If you love taking photographs and have a knack for getting professional-looking images, you can use your skills and expertise to sell photos online.

Websites like Depositphotos and iStockPhoto pay photographers to supply them with stock photos they can sell to writers, publications, and various online platforms.

According to recent reports, the best part about this side hustle is that you can get started with the equipment you already have. While you can use a professional camera if you want to, many smartphones take professional-quality photos.

Recent findings suggest that earning a bank bonus is another way to earn money without a regular job, but you’ll need an upfront investment to get started. Most bonus offers require you to deposit a specific amount of money and keep it in your account for up to 12 months.

You may also be required to set up direct deposit to earn a bank bonus, and other terms and conditions may apply.

According to recent reports, where can you find the best bank bonuses? While bonus offers constantly change, you can start by checking with banks like Chase, HSBC, Radius Bank, and Wells Fargo.

Flipping furniture requires some upfront legwork and potentially even some artistic talent, but you can earn a solid income with this strategy if you know what you’re doing.

Essentially, this side hustle requires you to shop at thrift stores, garage sales, and online platforms to find furniture that will ultimately sell for more than you paid.

From there, you can sell the furniture as-is or clean it up and paint it with the goal of fetching an even higher price.

You can make money driving for Uber or Lyft on your own time, picking and choosing the days and hours you want to work.

Not only is rideshare work one of the most flexible side hustles, but you can earn $20 per hour and more with tips.

Sources indicate that if you are low on free time but still want to make money without a job, consider selling stuff you don’t need. An array of online platforms makes it a breeze, although some platforms work better for selling.

For example, you can use Poshmark to earn money selling used clothing and accessories, while used electronics tend to sell best on platforms like eBay.com, Decluttr, BuyBackWorld, and Gazelle.

If you have home decor, furniture, or workout equipment to sell, you’ll almost always do better unloading those items locally on Facebook Marketplace.

Recent findings suggest that starting a YouTube channel is another way to earn money without a job, but that doesn’t mean it’s not work. The fact is, that creating quality videos and building an audience takes a lot of creativity and time. Plus, not everyone who tries to build a YouTube channel will succeed.

Recent findings suggest that that mentioned, you can earn income without a regular job. I know because I have done it with my YouTube channel, Wealth Hacker.

How much you can earn on YouTube varies quite a bit, but it’s possible to earn thousands of dollars per month. If you’re curious about monetizing videos, my in-depth guide will show you how to make money on YouTube.

Sources indicate that donating plasma is a unique way to earn money without a job, although it’s not very glamorous. DonatingPlasma.org makes it easy to find plasma donation centers in your area, and you can earn as much as $100 for your first donation.

Recent findings suggest that that remarked, subsequent plasma donations typically earn closer to $50. You’ll also be limited by the number of times you can donate plasma within a month. However, it’s possible to use this side gig to earn an extra $500 per month, which you can use to supplement your primary income.

According to recent reports, if you are willing to complete various tasks that help regular workers do their jobs, consider becoming a crowd worker. This gig will have you finishing up to-do lists of jobs that don’t require specific technical skills.

For example, you may get paid to proofread documents, label images, update a resume, complete a form, or complete a data entry assignment.

Several platforms help you find crowd-working gigs, but the best ones include Microworkers and Clickworker.

Recent findings suggest that if you want to do something simple that will get you moving, consider delivering groceries using apps like Instacart or Shipt. You get paid hourly, plus tips and all you have to do is head to the store, purchase groceries according to a list, and deliver them to people in your neighborhood.

The gig is extremely flexible, similar to driving for Uber or Lyft.

Recent findings suggest that another non-job gig lets you get paid to deliver packages for Amazon.com. You can do this through a platform called Amazon Flex, which promises its drivers anywhere from $18 to $25 per hour.

Recent findings suggest that unlike a regular Amazon job, Flex lets you pick the day and the hours you want to work. To get started, you need to create a free account, get approved, and start reserving blocks of time you want to deliver packages.

Recent findings suggest that finally, you can earn money by selling unwanted or unused gift cards in your possession. This hustle is made easy thanks to platforms like GiftDeals.com and CardCash.com.

You won’t get the total value of your gift cards, but you should get 90% or more of the gift card balance for each card you sell. While selling gift cards for less than their total value may not seem ideal, it’s better than not using them and getting nothing in return.

Finally, you can earn small amounts of money by signing up with the best online survey sites. Not only is this side hustle as easy as it gets, but you can participate and get paid during your spare time and even on your phone.

Other online survey sites to check out include the following:.

There you have it, 26 ways to make money without a job. While many of the jobs on our list won’t replace your 9-5, they can be a great way to increase your income so you can pay off debt or break the cycle of living paycheck to paycheck.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, every on-time student loan payment builds your credit, just as car loan payments do. A federal loan gives you 90 days before a late payment reaches your credit reports, where it stays for seven years. Set up autopay now, and if a payment gets hard to make, switch repayment plans before you miss one.

When missed federal student loan payments returned to credit reports in early 2025, more than 2.2 million newly delinquent borrowers saw their scores fall more than 100 points, the Federal Reserve Bank of Upcoming York found.

Recent findings suggest that paid on time, a student loan helps your score most through payment history, which makes up 35% of a FICO score, and the years you carry it lengthen your credit history. A substantial balance isn’t scored like credit card debt near its limit. FICO compares what you still owe with what you borrowed, and paying it down counts in your favor.

Sources indicate that the servicer that bills a federal loan reports a missed payment to the credit bureaus once it’s 90 days late. Most federal loans default after 270 days without a payment, and the default goes on your reports too. Private lenders set their own rules, and some report a missed payment as soon as 30 days after it’s due.

It has been revealed that autopay makes each payment on time even if you forget, and the Education Department trims the rate for borrowers who use it. If the payment is too high, an income-driven plan sets it from your income and family size, and a deferment or forbearance temporarily pauses payments, though interest usually keeps building. Either one, set up before a payment is 90 days late, keeps it off your reports. After a default, rehabilitation, nine affordable monthly payments agreed with the loan’s holder, removes the default from your credit history but not the late payments before it.

It has been revealed that picture two graduates, each with $30,000 in federal loans and three months between jobs. One skips three payments, so by her fourth due date the first is about 90 days late and goes on her reports for seven years. The other calls her servicer first and switches to an income-driven strategy based on what she earns, so she never misses one.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that A cashless store is legal in most of the U.S., since federal law leaves it to each store whether to take cash.
  • According to recent reports, the “legal tender for all debts, public and private” line on every bill reads like a rule that stores must take it.
  • Legal tender means cash is a valid way to pay a debt, the Federal Reserve explains, but no federal law requires a private business to take it for a purchase.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that A cashless store is legal in most of the U.S., since federal law leaves it to each store whether to take cash. But 10 states, and cities such as Philadelphia and San Francisco, require most stores and restaurants to accept it. Check your state’s and city’s rules before you count on paying cash, and carry a backup card.

According to recent reports, the “legal tender for all debts, public and private” line on every bill reads like a rule that stores must take it. It isn’t one.

Legal tender means cash is a valid way to pay a debt, the Federal Reserve explains, but no federal law requires a private business to take it for a purchase.

In November 2026, the Pew Research Center counted 10 states that make most in-person businesses take cash: Massachusetts, Latest Jersey, Rhode Island, Colorado, Connecticut, Oregon, Delaware, Montana, New York, and Maryland. New York’s law took effect in March 2026 and Maryland’s in October, and Illinois’s starts in January 2028. Pew counted 10 cities and counties too, including Philadelphia, San Francisco, Detroit, Miami-Dade County, and Washington, D.C.

Before you insist on paying cash, know what your law leaves out. The laws mostly cover stores and restaurants, but Connecticut’s law exempts membership warehouse clubs such as Costco, Oregon’s exempts farmers markets and roadside stands, and Fresh York’s lets a store turn down bills over $20. Some, New York’s among them, also exempt a store with a kiosk that turns cash into a prepaid card, which in New York must be free to use.

If a store your law covers still refuses your cash, ask for a manager and mention the law. If that fails, report the store to the office that enforces it, such as Upcoming York’s attorney general.

Recent findings suggest that where no law applies, a card-only venue may offer one of those kiosks anyway. Say a stadium’s concession stands take only cards and its kiosk turns your $20 into a prepaid card. Look for a fee on its screen before you insert the bill, and use up the balance, since some prepaid cards charge a fee once they sit unused.

Keep a debit card from a free checking account, or a prepaid card with no monthly fee, in your wallet next to your cash, so you can still pay where cash isn’t taken.

  • Thumbtack’s catering cost guide puts a caterer’s buffet at about $23 to $25 a guest, so feeding 40 people that way runs $920 to $1,000.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that A significant party’s cost is mostly food and drink multiplied by your guest list, so set a per-guest budget before you invite anyone. Then start at 2 p.m. or 8 p.m., when guests have already eaten, and make it a potluck so each family brings a side.

Thumbtack’s catering cost guide puts a caterer’s buffet at about $23 to $25 a guest, so feeding 40 people that way runs $920 to $1,000.

In a recent development, timing is the cheapest fix, because guests who have just eaten want snacks, not a full plate. Marquette University’s event planning tips say 6 to 8 appetizers a guest are enough at a late-afternoon or late-evening reception, against 10 over the lunch hour.

Then split the menu with your guests. A potluck sign-up that gives each family a kind of dish, such as salad, chips, fruit, or dessert, keeps you from getting five bowls of pasta salad. “Bring your own drinks” on the invitation covers the beer and wine.

Work from the per-guest number. A 2 p.m. graduation open house for 40 with a $250 budget has about $6 a guest to spend. Say pork shoulder is on sale for about $2.20 a pound. Twenty pounds costs about $45 and cooks down to roughly 10 pounds of meat, a quarter pound for each of 40 sandwiches. The rest of the list, from buns and lemonade to paper goods, a fruit tray, and a sheet cake, fits in the remaining $205, while families bring the sides.

Holiday hosts can save more by buying the Thanksgiving turkey from the grocery ads and spending New Year’s Eve at home rather than going out.

Send the invitation as one group text with the start time, a link to the sign-up sheet, and “bring your own drinks” on the last line.

Having more than one type of debt is common, and that’s especially true once you graduate from college and start your first “real job.” You may have credit card debt, an auto loan, and a mortgage payment to make once you buy your first home. It’s also common to have other random debts to cover, including student loans.

Sources indicate that if you’re like many who took out loans during college, you will likely be paying them off after you graduate. In fact, 82% of students who borrowed loans expect to be making payments post-graduation, according to a recent College Ave Student Loans survey.

That said, you’ll want to make sure you’re balancing debt repayment with your savings goals along the way.

You’ll also want to make sure you’re paying down debts in the optimal order, or in a way that will help you save the most money on interest as possible while aligning with your goals. Which debts should you pay off first? Here’s a rundown of how to get the best results:.

No matter which types of debt you have, credit card debt should be your first priority. Why? Because credit card debt is likely the most expensive debt you have by far.

Federal Reserve data reveals the average credit card interest rate on accounts assessed interest came in at around 22% as of May 2023, yet your credit card could easily be charging higher rates than the average.

To save as much money as possible, you should strive to pay as much as you can toward high-interest credit card bills each month. You can also pay down credit card debt faster with the help of a debt consolidation loan or a 0% APR balance transfer credit card.

Industry observers note that other unsecured debts like personal loan debt should come next in the debt payoff pecking order. After all, unsecured debts tend to have higher interest rates than secured debts like auto loans. In fact, the Federal Reserve also reported that the average interest rate on a 24-month personal loan came in at 11.48% as of May 2023, compared to the average rate of 7.81% on a 60-month auto loan.

Ideally, you’ll start paying more toward personal loan debt and other unsecured debts after all credit card debt is entirely paid off, although you should make at least the minimum payment on all your bills throughout the entire process.

According to recent reports, the next debt you’ll want to tackle is your student loans. I suggest focusing on these loans after other unsecured debts, since federal student loans (and many private student loans) come with low fixed interest rates and monthly payments that will not change over time. If you have federal student loans, you may even want to look into income-driven repayment aims.

In a recent development, if you’re hoping to pay down student loans faster or just want to save money on interest, you can also consider refinancing your student loans to get a shorter repayment timeline, a lower monthly payment, or both. Just remember that refinancing federal student loans can mean losing access to income-driven repayment looks and federal protections like deferment and forbearance.

Once you have paid off or substantially paid down all your other debts, you can focus your efforts on secured debts you have like mortgage loans and auto loans. These debts should be dealt with last since they are secured with collateral and tend to offer lower interest rates as a result. For example, you can consider paying more than the minimum on your mortgage, a car loan, or both until they’re paid off completely.

Then again, you may want to pay off debts with extremely low interest rates as slowly as possible to free up more cash flow for living expenses and investments. If you took out a mortgage in January of 2021 when the average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed rate home loan was as low as 2.65%, for example, it makes sense to make the minimum payment on that debt and invest your extra cash instead.

In a recent development, it’s crucial to make sure you balance debt repayment with other financial considerations. After all, focusing too much on debt repayment early in life can leave you behind when it comes to investing for retirement or saving up for a first home.

While you’ll want to eliminate credit card debt and other high-interest debts as quickly as you can, even if you have to stop saving and investing for a while, you can pay down student loan debt and secured debts at a slower pace while saving and investing for the future along the way.

According to recent reports, finally, make sure you have adequate emergency savings throughout your entire debt payoff journey, or that you begin saving for emergencies as soon as you can. Without a fully funded emergency fund, you can end up relying on credit cards and other loans to get by and ruin your debt payoff progress in the process.

How much should you save? While most experts recommend having an emergency fund that can cover three to six months of expenses, it’s okay to start small if you have to.

Having more than one type of debt is how it works for most people, especially when you’re young and in the early stages of your career. When it comes to paying it off, however, you’ll want to make sure you have a concrete plan that can help you reduce interest charges and get where you want to be.

Focusing on credit card debt and other unsecured debts first always makes sense, since these debts aren’t secured by an asset and tend to charge much higher interest rates. You can focus on student loans next, followed by other secured debts you have like a home loan or car loan.

Industry observers note that in the meantime, make sure you have an adequate emergency fund and invest in it for retirement. After all, debt won’t last forever if you’re serious about repayment, and saving and investing early can help you benefit from compound interest and avoid using credit cards for surprise expenses. Creating a budget to track these factors is your best bet.

If you need help creating one, or simply don’t know where to start, use this budget worksheet as your guide – you’ll reach financial freedom in no time.

It has been revealed that A couple of years ago, Mr. Money Mustache lost some credibility among the faithful when he wrote this blog post about actually trying to spend a bit more money, while buying a Tesla as the first step in that program.

I thought to myself at the time,.

Sources indicate that “I’m such an enlightened middle-aged Badass, adjusting habits and realigning myself at the snap of my fingers. Onward to the next forty eight years of the Good Life!”.

So, two years passed with an even greater feeling of abundance. I had a marvelous time traveling everywhere and spending money like I thought a proper wealthy person would do.

I dined out in stylish restaurants, booked hotels based on their niceness rather than their cheapness, paid extra to sit in the “reduced torture” seats of the airplanes, and gave zero fucks about paying double for groceries if I happened to be in a Whole Foods rather than my usual Sam’s Club and Costco (and yes I treat myself to memberships at both warehouse stores!).

Among the highlights, my son and I have worked our way though a nice selection of late night EDM concerts and three Meowwolf art venues including a Christmas Day road trip from our winter home in Tempe Arizona to Las Vegas last year. And having spent much of the year as a single man, I had a wide open schedule to just meet up with friends, explore fresh places and meet new people as opportunities came up. It felt like a year of adventurous transition, which means it felt like much more than twelve months.

Sources indicate that with all this flashy spending, I was sure my budget must have crept back into full American Consumer territory. But I was having too much fun to bother adding it all up to check.

Until recently, when I was doing another round of informal coaching for a friend and we both decided to tally our spending for the past year to compare notes.

When I finally finished sorting all of those transactions into a spreadsheet and hit the “sum” button, the results surprised me.

While my overall spending had indeed increased (especially in travel-related categories), the massive-picture effect was still pretty minimal. Depending on how I account for things like the car and my business expenses, my spending went from $20,000 to about $30,000 (plus the usual hidden subsidy of a paid-off house.).

This level could still be sustained by a $1 million investment nest egg. Since my investments are quite a bit higher than that (especially after these recent years of crazy economic growth and the never-ending stock market rally), I’m still way under budget.

Although I still “failed” to really increase my spending to the MMM-recommended levels for old wealthy people, this still makes me happy, because I have genuinely had more fun with the abundance mindset, and I can keep trying more life experiments in the coming years.

It has been revealed that as we covered in the 2019 article on the idea of an Optimization Council, it’s always a good idea to compare our spending, tips and tricks on how to get the most out of life. Almost twenty years into early retirement, this is where I have landed so far, although I’m always learning and open to feedback.

Anyway, let’s cut the wistful commentary and get into the budget.

Sources indicate that in summary: Wow, how interesting! When we compare this to my 2019 post on that year’s spending, it’s only a bit higher even after all the inflation we have seen in recent years. I spent more on travel and fun, but less on home renovation – partly because I was away so much I didn’t have as much time to work on my house. The health insurance is a new cost too since I was self-insured back then.

My budget is notably missing the biggest expense for most people, which is housing costs. This is because I paid off my house long ago, and I also love working on and taking care of my own home, which means there are no bills for lawn mowing, plumbers, tree pruning or handyman services.

This strategy is not for everyone, and it’s not even the optimum financial one for me – I would have been better off taking out the biggest mortgage I could get at 3% back in the sweet borrowing times of 2021, and putting all that principal to work in stock index funds where it would have almost doubled since then. But I still get a great peace of mind from just having no mortgage payment, and there’s really no better way to use your money than to buy such good feelings. Also, I get a secondary benefit of not having to buy house insurance, which saves me another $2000 per year, boosting my effective return on that payoff.

First of all, the biggest money saving factor of good health and good luck has continued, meaning I’ve still had no actual medical expenses. But I still do maintain two layers of health care support which together feel very much like the ultimate version of health insurance: a membership with a top of the line Direct Primary Care (DPC) medical clinic ($107 per month) plus a high-deductible plan ($201) with a health sharing organization called Sedera.

The combined cost of $308 per month is less than the cheapest Bronze strategy in the field of standard health insurance, yet I get personalized support with zero deductible for almost all typical medical needs, plus some protection from larger medical bills if my good luck runs out.

But as a disclaimer, I’m not an expert on medical needs and health insurance because I’ve had so little experience with the system. And the highest priority in my life is arranging my days for maximum health to give me the best chance of keeping it this way.

When it comes down to it, money is a tool for survival and if we’re lucky, self actualization. So I’m always asking myself if there’s anything I can change or improve to make the most of this good fortune.

I also try to keep in mind an interesting principle of happiness, which indicates that,.

Fixing your persistent problems is more effective than just doubling down on things that are already good in your life.

For me, there are already a lot of good things which don’t need improving. My family, friends, relationships, health, food and daily activities are pretty much as good as I could imagine.

Sources indicate that the only annoyance I can think of is physical chaos: I have a lot of space-intensive hobbies like construction and music, and I currently live in a pretty small house which is basically maxed out. I could really use a doubling of my workshop space from the current 2-car, 440 square foot garage to maybe a thousand or so.

Recent findings suggest that but I also love where I live and wouldn’t want to give up my views, neighbors or current place. So I’ll keep optimizing what I’ve got unless some perfect opportunity comes up for a bigger place right on my block.

In the longer run, a mountain compound with its own cliffs and stream are also on my “maybe” list. But once again, my days and life are already overbooked with joyful things. My existing house and our HQ Coworking space already have long to-do lists. Would I actually be happier if I added another place to my portfolio? So I keep this idea on the shelf until I’m willing to trade it for another existing commitment – like selling my house or the coworking space.

But for now, I’m just extremely excited to blaze into 2025 with loads abundance and piles of challenging stuff on my to-do list. And I wish you the same!

In the Comments: Where are you at on this spectrum of stinginess versus abundance mentality, and fulfilment versus longing in life?

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that before you buy a rental or turn your home into one, add up every cost of owning it, from the mortgage and taxes to repairs, empty months, and management. Go ahead only if the rent covers them all with room to spare and you’re ready to screen tenants, follow landlord-tenant laws, and take repair calls.

Industry observers note that rent that beats the mortgage payment doesn’t make a rental profitable. The gap has to pay for everything else the property costs.

Say a couple rents out their old condo, and its mortgage payment, property taxes and insurance included, is $1,600 a month. At $1,900 in rent, they expect to clear $300 a month, or $3,600 a year. Then two empty months cost $3,800 in rent, and a new water heater and a cleaning between tenants cost $3,200. They end the year $3,400 behind.

Before you buy, or rent out the home you’re leaving, budget for four more costs:.

In a recent development, depreciation lowers the tax on your rent because you deduct the building’s cost, though not the land’s, over 27.5 years. The IRS also lets owners who approve tenants and repairs deduct up to $25,000 a year of rental losses from other income, an allowance that shrinks to nothing at higher incomes. Any loss beyond it waits for a later year.

Industry observers note that A rental is also a job. Someone has to screen applicants, follow fair housing rules and your state’s security deposit and eviction laws, and take the midnight call about a leak. That’s you, or a manager you pay. A real estate fund gives you a stake in property without that work, so count your time as a cost too.

Become a landlord only if the rent still leaves money after every cost above, with repairs and management figured at the high end of their ranges.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Open a GoFundMe Giving Fund if you itemize and blueprint to give cash, stocks, or exchange-traded funds over a few years, since it charges no administrative fee and lets you contribute or grant as little as $5. Skip it for crypto or private tech giant shares, and give straight to charities instead if you take the standard deduction.

GoFundMe Giving Funds is a donor-advised fund for givers who want a tax deduction now and time to choose charities later, run since June 2025 by GoFundMe Giving Fund, a 501(c)(3) public charity separate from GoFundMe. It charges no administrative fee, where DAFgiving360 charges 0.60% a year on the first $500,000, which works out to $60 a year on a $10,000 balance.

Industry observers note that itemizers who give cash, stocks, or ETFs over a few years lose none of their balance to an administrative fee here. If you take the standard deduction, give straight to charities instead, because starting in 2026 up to $1,000 of cash gifts ($2,000 on a joint return) is deductible without itemizing, and contributions to a donor-advised fund don’t qualify.

Learn more about GoFundMe Giving Funds.

Sources indicate that certificates of Deposit (CDs) work similarly to online savings accounts or money market accounts in terms of offering great returns with zero risk. The difference is, CDs “lock your money up” for a specified period of time. To access your funds before the term ends, you’ll have to pay a penalty.

Industry observers note that although CDs offer less liquidity than a regular checking account or savings account, you might get a higher rate of return with this financial product. This is especially true if you open a CD account with a longer timeline; for example, a 60-month CD instead of a 12-month CD.

Picture this: you're settling into a lie-flat business class seat somewhere over the Atlantic, a glass of something cold in hand, knowing that in 48 hours you'll be waking up in Istanbul — and then, a few days later, continuing onward to Bangkok. Two bucket-list cities. One award booking. One points balance. This is what the Aeroplan stopover sweet spot feels like in practice. It's not a trick or a loophole — it's a deliberately designed feature of Air Canada's Aeroplan program that the vast majority of travelers simply don't know exists. And that gap between awareness and reality is exactly where the ChooseFI community finds its edge. Here's the math that should make your jaw drop. A business class itinerary from North America to Istanbul with a continuing flight onward to Bangkok — two long-haul segments, lie-flat seats, Star Alliance lounges at every connection — would cost somewhere between **$6,000 and $15,000 in cash**. That's a realistic retail range depending on season and how far out you book. Most people never consider it a possibility for a family vacation or a milestone trip because the sticker price puts it in a different universe. With Aeroplan, you're booking that same itinerary — the same seats, the same lounges, the same Turkish Airlines or Thai Airways product — for **75,000 Aeroplan points**. At the low end of the cash price range, that's already **8 cents per point**. At the high end, you're extracting **20 cents per point** from a currency that most people earned by putting groceries on a credit card. The pricing inefficiency here is structural. Aeroplan's partner award chart prices long-haul business class at a fixed rate regardless of cash fare fluctuations. When business class prices spike — around holidays, during peak travel seasons, during major events — your points cost stays exactly the same. You're insulated from the market. That's the FI mindset applied to travel: you've already paid for the trip in points, slowly accumulated through everyday spending, and now you're simply redeeming the stored value. The stopover itself is nearly free. Aeroplan charges just 5,000 extra miles to add a stopover city to a one-way award. That means your Istanbul layover becomes a multi-day stay — at zero additional points cost beyond that small add-on — and you haven't booked a second award at all. One booking. Two destinations. That's the entire premise, and once you see it, you can't unsee it.

The mechanism behind this sweet spot is elegantly simple once you understand it, but it requires knowing three things that most travelers don't: how Aeroplan's routing rules work, what a stopover actually is in the context of an award ticket, and why Star Alliance's global network makes this scalable to almost any destination pair you can imagine.

When Aeroplan relaunched its loyalty program in 2020, it did something remarkable: it eliminated fuel surcharges entirely and published a partner award chart with fixed pricing for flights on Star Alliance carriers. This is critical. When you book Turkish Airlines business class through Aeroplan, you pay the Aeroplan fixed chart rate — not what Turkish Airlines would charge in its own currency or miles program, and not the inflated cash price. That fixed chart is the engine of this redemption.

In a recent development, for long-haul international business class, Aeroplan's chart prices routing through multiple regions based on your origin and destination — not every intermediate stop. This is the aha moment. Aeroplan determines your award price based on where your journey starts and where it ends, and then allows you to add a stopover in between for just 5,000 additional miles. The stopover city is priced as a pass-through for the purpose of calculating your award zone, not as a second trip.

Sources indicate that on a one-way Aeroplan award, you're permitted to add a free stopover — meaning you can stay in an intermediate city for any length of time before continuing to your final destination. That 5,000-mile add-on is essentially the cost of a full additional destination. Compare that to booking a second one-way award from Istanbul to Bangkok, which would cost you another 40,000–55,000 Aeroplan points in business class. The math is decisive.

Recent findings suggest that the routing must be geographically sensible — you can't fly backwards across the globe — but Aeroplan's allowance for multi-segment itineraries through Star Alliance hubs gives you enormous flexibility. Istanbul (IST) is a Turkish Airlines hub. Bangkok (BKK) is served by Thai Airways and several Star Alliance carriers. Both are Star Alliance partners. Both are bookable through Aeroplan at fixed chart rates with no fuel surcharges.

Having Chase Ultimate Rewards as your primary earning currency means you can search, find space, and transfer points before the availability window closes. The 1:1 ratio across all four programs means no conversion math — every point you earn translates directly to one Aeroplan mile.

Booking an Aeroplan stopover award in business class is genuinely one of the more complex redemptions in the travel rewards world, but it becomes manageable when you break it into distinct phases. Here's exactly how to do it.

Start by deciding on your two destinations. Aeroplan stopovers work best when your intermediate city is a major Star Alliance hub that lies geographically between your origin and final destination. Classic combinations include North America to Istanbul (Turkish Airlines hub) continuing to Southeast Asia, or North America to a European hub continuing to the Middle East or East Africa. Your stopover city should be somewhere you genuinely want to spend 2–5 days — this is a real trip, not just a layover.

It has been revealed that this is the most important and most time-consuming step. You need to find saver-level business class availability on both segments independently before you book.

Industry observers note that once you've confirmed availability on both segments, go to aeroplan.com and use the multi-city search function. Enter your full itinerary — origin, stopover city with your intended layover dates, and final destination.

Once you've confirmed the award is bookable and are ready to complete the reservation:.

Sources indicate that complete your booking on aeroplan.com or with a phone agent, confirm the stopover is properly reflected in your itinerary, and save every confirmation email. Verify your seats on each carrier's website immediately after booking.

A stopover is an intentional break in your journey lasting more than 24 hours at a connecting city. Most airlines treat stopovers as separate tickets, charging full price for each segment. Aeroplan is one of the few programs that allows a free stopover on round-trip awards, letting you explore a connecting city for days before continuing to your final destination. This is fundamentally different from a layover, which is a brief connection of a few hours at an airport. The stopover must be in a city served by a Star Alliance carrier on your routing, and the key is that Aeroplan prices the entire itinerary as one award, not two.

Leverage the open-jaw rule too. Aeroplan also allows open-jaw routing — fly into one city, depart from another. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that A home workout plan needs no trainer or paid app. Federal exercise guidelines call for at least 150 minutes of brisk walking or other moderate cardio a week, plus strength work on two or more days. Put each session on your calendar, train with body weight and household items, and add reps or minutes every week or two.

It has been revealed that the 150 minutes and the two strength days come from the Department of Health and Human Services’ Physical Activity Guidelines for Americans. They tell you how much exercise is enough, which is part of what a trainer or a paid app charges for.

A walk counts as brisk at 2.5 miles per hour or faster, and 75 minutes of vigorous activity like running meets the cardio target on its own. For strength work, the guidelines say to do each move until one more repetition would be hard, and a single set of 8 to 12 repetitions per move is effective.

Five moves cover every major muscle group: squats and lunges for your legs and hips, push-ups for your chest, shoulders, and arms, rows for your back, and a plank for your core. Do push-ups against a kitchen counter until you can do 8 from the floor. For rows, bend forward and pull a gallon jug of water or a backpack loaded with books toward your ribs, and wear the backpack for squats once body-weight squats feel easy.

For cardio, pick what you’ll keep doing, whether that’s brisk walks, runs, or a free workout video. Then give every session a day and a time, as you would an appointment. A 40-year-old could do 25-minute strength sessions on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday and 50-minute brisk walks on Tuesday, Thursday, and Saturday. That’s 150 minutes of cardio and three strength days, with Sunday off, at no cost.

In a recent development, write down the repetitions for each move and the minutes of each cardio session, in a notebook, a free app, or the printable strategy from the federal Move Your Way activity planner. Every week or two, add two repetitions, a second set, more weight in the backpack, or five minutes of cardio, since the guidelines call for raising activity gradually over weeks to months.

If you’ve been inactive, start smaller, with 10-minute walks and one strength day a week, and build to the full blueprint over several weeks.

Picture a bookkeeper who caps her costs at $500 for software and a website, then does the books for three local shops on weekends. After a year, the clients pay enough that she cuts her job to part time.

Recent findings suggest that expect mistakes, like a price set too low or a client who pays late. On a small budget each one costs little, so fix it rapidly instead of trying to prevent every one.

Write the three limits down today, before you buy anything for the business.

It has been revealed that monarch Money offers robust financial planning tools: budgets, goals, net worth tracking, and more, with subscription visibility included in the package. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On-time phone and utility payments rarely reach your credit report, so they don’t help your score. Link the bank account you pay them from to Experian Boost, a free tool that adds them to your Experian report. It’s most worth doing when your credit history is short or your score sits just under a lender’s cutoff.

These bills usually reach a credit report only when one goes unpaid and lands in collections, the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau states.

According to recent reports, boost doesn’t wait for the phone company or utility to report. It reads two years of payments in the account you connect and lets you pick which qualifying bills go on your Experian report. Experian highlights you right away whether your FICO Score 8, one version of the FICO score, went up.

Sources indicate that only your Experian report gets those payments, so lenders checking your reports at the other two credit bureaus, Equifax and TransUnion, won’t see the gain. Experian also says not every lender uses a score that Boost affects, and most mortgage lenders don’t.

Industry observers note that payments by check or through apps like Venmo don’t count. Some rent paid online counts too, though Boost is just one of several ways to get rent reported. You also need enough history for a FICO Score, meaning at least one account active six months or more and one reported in the last six.

Take a renter with one credit card who links the account she pays her phone and electric bills from. Boost finds two years of on-time payments on both. Experian notes people whose score rose gained 14 points on average. The trade-off is letting Experian see that account’s payment history. Some scores also stay flat or even drop. If hers drops, she can disconnect, and Experian says the score should return to where it was.

Connect your bill-paying account now, ahead of any credit application, and leave it linked so Experian keeps checking for latest on-time payments.

#33806. Wow, have you seen the stock market lately?
